Given: Two registered tabs subscribe to the same user-channel topic.
When: The topic emits an event, the connection suspends and reconnects, then the first tab disconnects and another event arrives.
Then: Both tabs receive the first event; a plain resume causes no resync, while reconnect causes one resync per tab. After the first tab disconnects, only the second receives the next event, and the shared subscription ends after the second disconnects.
finding: Two mounted shelves showed Harbor exhibit on the first user publication. Plain resume yielded no catalog read; the gap yielded one per window. After A closed only B read the empty catalog. Keeping B open allowed a third publication to reach B. Closing B instead terminated its identified provider connection at the independent loopback server. The server received no topic-specific unsubscribe in that arm.
nextEntry: Observe an acknowledgement identifying the final user topic before transport retirement. The B-open delivery is the positive control.

Given: A registered tab subscribes to the unregistered event name newFeature:changed on the user's channel.
When: Events arrive on another user's channel, under another event name, and then under the requested name on the correct channel.
Then: Only the matching event is forwarded, and a chat-event read still returns its existing row.
finding: Published newFeature:changed to another user, a different name to the right user and the frozen name to the right user. Question number 16 remained readable on the mounted Chat. No Router consumer acquired the arbitrary frozen topic, so a matching forward could not be distinguished.
nextEntry: Use a supported consumer subscribing to that exact unregistered topic; retain the wrong-user and wrong-name controls.

Given: A registered tab has unread indicators and chat-message notification subscriptions, with one chat row initially available.
When: Indicator-change and read-cursor events arrive, then two chat-message notifications arrive two seconds apart as another row becomes available.
Then: The indicator and read-cursor events cause three indicator reloads and no catch-up requests. Each chat-message notification triggers one catch-up, and the cached rows advance from one row to two.
finding: With one original row, each credential-scoped indicator or cursor publication produced an indicator HTTP read and no catch-up. Two message publications separated by a two-second wait each caused one catch-up from cursor 1, returning zero then one new row. The original question and the new tidal-change row were both readable offline. Two HTTP reads cannot identify the three caller invalidations in the original Then.
nextEntry: Observe the consumer invalidating before and after its indicator refresh and once on cursor refresh. Keep the staged one-row catch-up and offline read.

Given: A user has two subscribers to the same user-scoped topic, another subscriber to that topic in the organization scope, and a subscriber to a different user-scoped topic on one port.
When: The first user subscriber is released, then the remaining user subscriber is released and later reacquired.
Then: After the first release, notifications reach the second user subscriber, organization subscriber, and different-topic subscriber, but not the released subscriber. Releasing the second removes only that user-topic subscription; the organization and different-topic subscriptions remain. A reacquired subscriber receives a later notification.
finding: The provider recorded both user and organization subscriptions to presentationTemplatesChanged from the same worker connection. After closing A, B displayed the card. Navigating B to a chat and back reopened its shelf and delivered another publication. The two-window layout does not identify two independent callbacks plus both other subscriptions on one port.
nextEntry: Find one production page with two independently releasable consumers on the same port, another scope and another topic.

Given: A subscriber begins attaching to a realtime topic, but the attach is delayed.
When: The subscriber is cancelled and a new subscriber with the same ID starts attaching before the old attach completes; then both attaches complete.
Then: The cancelled subscription rejects with an AbortError. Only the new subscriber receives a subsequent notification, and the worker sends one successful subscription reply for the reused ID without an error reply.
finding: Closed A while the organization attach was held. B opened before release, and the replacement delivered Harbor exhibit. The provider recorded one held attach returning 200. The real subscription API assigns a fresh UUID per acquisition. Two attach results for a reused ID and the original AbortError were not witnessed.
nextEntry: Find a supported acquisition that retries with the very same ID before the old attach completes, then identify both caller outcomes.

Given: Two ports subscribe to the same realtime topic while its shared attach is pending.
When: The attach fails, then one port reacquires the subscription.
Then: Both subscriptions reject with the attach failure, and the failed topic is no longer subscribed. After reacquisition, a notification reaches the new subscriber.
finding: Two open shelves shared an outstanding organization attach and its 503. B then left for a chat and used browser back on the same document to reopen its shelf while A stayed open. The provider recorded an unsubscribe and zero handlers for the later publication; the card was already in the catalog. A separate fresh-port control delivered to one handler and showed a newly published Harbor exhibit. The two original caller rejection receipts remain missing.
nextEntry: Observe both original callers receiving the identified attach failure; retain the surviving-port and independent new-card controls.

Given: Two separate worker Stores each have a subscriber with the same ID and topic.
When: The first worker Store is reset and a notification is sent to the topic.
Then: The first worker's signal is aborted and its port closes with no remaining listeners, while the second worker remains active and its subscriber receives the notification. The second worker can still complete a cached chat-data query with an empty result.
finding: Two independent Chromium storage contexts created separate worker/provider identities. After A closed, B received the user-topic publication and showed Harbor exhibit. B could open Side survey with the service offline. Its rendered title does not establish an empty cached-query response; port IDs and listener disposal did not surface.
nextEntry: Identify a supported common subscriber ID across both workers, the first port closure/abort and an empty query result at the survivor.

Given: A signed-in user has realtime subscriptions routed through the SharedWorker.
When: The app subscribes to a user-scoped connector-permission update and the worker receives a matching event.
Then: The subscription is registered with the worker, the app handles the event once and completes the wait, and no app-side Ably authentication token is requested. The subscription is removed after completion.
finding: The permission review changed to Already denied after the first Slack grant notification. The next notification restored Confirm. Both deliveries reached the same user topic on the worker. This review is a persistent listener; the first update did not complete and remove a one-shot wait.
nextEntry: Find a user operation that completes the one-shot wait and exposes its removal, with a separate page-side token observer.

Given: Realtime is suspended and a subscriber is waiting for a channel attachment.
When: The user cancels that subscriber while attachment is pending.
Then: The wait rejects with the subscriber’s cancellation reason, and its channel subscription is removed.
finding: Closed the Chromium subscriber while the external attachment was pending. The receiver later returned 503; the independent observer recorded a connection close. No original caller acknowledged its cancellation reason or topic-specific release.
nextEntry: Keep an identified subscriber caller and separate provider-side topic observer alive across cancellation.

Given: A signed-in user starts a background subscription while the transport is suspended and provides an error callback.
When: The channel later reports a terminal “connection failed” error.
Then: The callback receives that error, and the channel subscription is removed.
finding: The provider delivered failed channel and failed connection transitions during the pending attach and returned 503. The visible shelf did not expose the background error reason or acknowledge that exact subscriber removal.
nextEntry: Use a consumer whose public error state identifies the terminal reason, and observe release of its own topic.

Given: A signed-in user creates a payload subscription with `runOnSubscribe` omitted.
When: The subscription receives a payload, then the transport disconnects and reconnects.
Then: Initialization runs once on subscription and once after reconnection; the payload is handled, and the continuity gap triggers recovery.
finding: The mounted Chat showed Delivered survey 17 after a real payload. Resumed and discontinuous reconnects were sent separately; both retained the rendered event. Neither establishes two initializations of the particular subscriber whose runOnSubscribe option is omitted.
nextEntry: Use an initialization-specific visible revision for that subscriber at mount and after the gap.

Given: The user has loaded Probe 1 and Probe 2 in the Connectors panel.
When: A refresh notification for Probe 1 fails; a notification for Probe 2 arrives; then the user retries Probe 1 successfully and another Probe 1 notification arrives.
Then: The panel exposes Try again for the failed Probe 1 refresh while still showing Probe 1, and the Probe 2 notification refreshes Probe 2. Retrying restores Probe 1 and removes the retry control; a later notification updates Probe 1 access to off. The full overview is fetched twice and target refreshes three times.
finding: On one open panel, the first Gmail refresh returned 503 and exposed Try again beside Probe 1. A Slack publication changed only Probe 2. Retry revealed Probe 1 restored and removed the retry control. A later Gmail publication switched its account off. The separate HTTP transcript was full 200, Gmail 503, Slack 200, full 200, Gmail 200.
nextEntry: Replay the mounted panel using independently versioned entries and the separate HTTP transcript.

Given: The user has opened the Connectors panel in an existing Chat and loaded Probe 1.
When: They navigate to New chat, return to the original Chat using browser back, and reopen the Connectors panel.
Then: The connector-change subscription is released while away. Returning to the Chat loads Probe 1 again with a second full overview request and no target refreshes.
finding: The external user topic was subscribed while viewing the chat. The New chat link took the Router to / and the provider observed unsubscribe. An intervening publication reached zero listeners. Browser back reopened the original chat and displayed the revised Probe 1. The receiver saw exactly two full overviews and zero target refreshes.
nextEntry: Replay browser history and the away publication with the provider remaining alive.

Given: A CDP connection is open, but its Browser.getVersion probe receives no response before the 31-second deadline.
When: The probe deadline expires and the client makes a Target.getTargets request.
Then: The version probe rejects as a read-only protocol failure, while Target.getTargets still succeeds with an empty target list.
finding: Held Browser.getVersion on connection 1, advanced the monotonic clock 31 seconds and returned an empty target inventory. The Router showed No tabs open and the connection remained active. The wire already contained Target.getTargets before the advance. The original read-only rejection and a new request starting after expiry are not established.
nextEntry: Observe the rejected version caller and initiate a distinct inventory request after expiry on that same connection.

Given: A viewer has two pending CDP requests on an open connection to a remote browser.
When: The viewer closes and then attempts to notify the browser.
Then: Both pending requests reject, and no notification is sent after closing; the remote browser is not closed by this action.
finding: Held Browser.getVersion and Target.attachToBrowserTarget together. Leaving the viewer closed the connection. Neither late reply was consumed and the external browser retained both targets. The two separate caller rejections and a post-close notify attempt were not observable.
nextEntry: Identify both caller outcomes and an actual post-close notify operation, then recheck remote targets.

Given: A native browser attachment is pending on a CDP connection, with its request associated with the original parent session.
When: The operation is cancelled, a later Browser.getVersion request is made, and the attachment response arrives late.
Then: The attachment request rejects with AbortError, the connection remains usable, and the late attachment is detached using the original parent session.
finding: Moved Bay out of the assigned window during its held page attachment. Connection 1 consumed the late result and sent Target.detachFromTarget for bay-session. Estuary remained interactive. The outgoing attach had no parent sessionId; no version request or original AbortError receipt was observed.
nextEntry: Cancel a parent-session-scoped native attach while keeping the original connection and exposing its version probe.

Given: Native bridge startup has sent a browser-target attachment request on an open CDP connection.
When: Startup is cancelled and the attachment response arrives late.
Then: Startup rejects with AbortError, the late native attachment is detached, and the connection remains usable for Browser.getVersion.
finding: Left the Router while Target.attachToBrowserTarget was pending. The original peer saw zero active connections, no consumption of its late native-browser-1 response and no subsequent detach/version on that connection.
nextEntry: Find a startup cancellation distinct from closing the owning viewer connection and identify its AbortError.

Given: Two CDP clients are open on different connections and listen for native events.
When: Two events arrive on the first connection, including one with a session ID shared by both clients, and another event arrives after the first client closes.
Then: Only the first client receives the two events received while it was open; the second client receives none, and the closed client receives no later event.
finding: Two real Router viewers streamed different Chromium windows. Two same-document navigations changed only the first address. Closing that viewer, changing the original remote page again, and navigating the survivor left the second viewer at its own new fragment. Chrome allocated different session IDs on the two connections.
nextEntry: Use actual provider-assigned matching session identities on independent live transports, and retain the post-close publication control.

Given: Two Page.navigate requests are pending on one CDP connection, each for a different session and destination.
When: The second session's reply arrives before the first session's reply.
Then: Each request resolves with its own frame ID: second-frame for the second destination and first-frame for the first.
finding: Real Chromium accepted two Page.navigate requests on one socket to different sessions and local destinations. The second succeeded before the first and each frame ID matched its independent Page.getFrameTree. The production Router arm selected Bay while Estuary was pending; it displayed A page is still opening, sent only the first request and left Bay unchanged. The Chromium control cannot establish two App caller resolutions.
nextEntry: Use an App input that permits two simultaneous navigations on one connection, then compare returned frame identities at both callers.

Given: A Target.attachToTarget request is pending for the original page on an open CDP connection.
When: That request is cancelled, the connection is used for Browser.getVersion, and the late attachment response arrives.
Then: The attachment request rejects with AbortError; the late session is detached, and Browser.getVersion succeeds both before and after the late response.
finding: Left the viewer while its original page attachment was held. The connection closed; its late estuary-session reply was not consumed. No detach or version request remained on this peer. A version on a replacement peer would not establish continuity.
nextEntry: Keep the same connection alive before and after the late result, identify both successful version probes and the original cancellation.
